nodes.name: Carbon cloth activation
nodes.procedure: The carbon cloth was cleaned ultrasonically by ethanol, acetone, and deionized water, respectively, for 10 min to remove grease and impurities on the surface, and then it was activated by nitric acid, and finally it was washed by deionized water and ethanol before dried at 25°C in an oven.
nodes.source_text: 2.3.1. Activation Method of Substrate Materials... carbon cloth was cleaned ultrasonically by ethanol, acetone, and deionized water

nodes.name: MOF growth on CC
nodes.procedure: Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O (0.291 g) was completely dissolved in 20 mL deionized water (denoted as "solution A"). 1 cm×1 cm pretreated CC substrate was fully immersed in "solution A" with continuously ultrasonic stirring for 5 min. 2-MIM (0.66 g) was dissolved in 20 mL deionized water and ultrasound for 2 min at 25°C to obtain "solution B." It was slowly poured into "solution A" before sufficiently dissolved, and the mixture was let stand for 12 h to obtain MOF@CC electrode (as ZIF-67@CC). It was softly washed with deionized water and dried at 25°C.

nodes.name: CoB electroless plating on MOF@CC
nodes.procedure: The mixtures of cobalt nitrate (Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, 1.25 g), sodium succinate (1.25 g), sodium sulfate (0.75 g), and DMAB (0.36 g) were dissolved in 50 mL deionized water ultrasonically to prepare an electroless plating solution. The molar ratio of Co to B was 1:0.66. Then the MOF-based carbon cloth was soaked in the electroless plating solution for 30 min at 25°C to prepare a CoB@MOF@CC catalytic electrode.

nodes.description: HER performance in alkaline simulated seawater
nodes.source_text: Based on the microstructure of the CoB@MOF@CC electrode ... a three-electrode configuration was used to test the catalytic performance in alkaline simulated seawater (1.0 M KOH + 0.5 M NaCl) at a scan rate of 5 mV s⁻¹ with 80% iR-correction ... The LSV curves of CoB@MOF@CC showed that the overpotential was only 57 mV at 10 mA cm⁻² ... at a current density of 500 mA cm⁻² was only 266 mV ... Tafel value of 69.1 mV dec⁻¹ ... charge transfer resistance of CoB@MOF@CC (R_ct = 4.91 Ω) ... C_dl value of 30.15 mF cm⁻² ... TOF value of CoB@MOF@CC (TOF = 0.0756 s⁻¹) ... electrolysis was maintained for over 2500 h at ... 500 mA cm⁻².

nodes.description: OER performance in alkaline simulated seawater
nodes.source_text: Similar to HER, the OER activity of the CoB@MOF@CC electrode was characterized at 25°C ... overpotential of CoB@MOF@CC at 10 mA cm⁻² was only 209 mV ... overpotential of 423 mV at 500 mA cm⁻² ... Tafel slopes ... CoB@MOF@CC (88.5 mV dec⁻¹) ... charge transfer resistance of CoB@MOF@CC (R_ct = 7.3 Ω) ... C_dl = 14.5 mF cm⁻² ... TOF value ... CoB@MOF@CC (0.021 s⁻¹) ... chronopotentiometry at a current density of 500 mA cm⁻² for 2500 h.

nodes.description: OWS performance in alkaline simulated seawater
nodes.source_text: Owing to the excellent HER and OER catalytic activities ... the OWS performance was tested in alkaline simulated seawater at 25°C. The voltage required by CoB@MOF@CC to achieve a current density of 10 mA cm⁻² was only 1.49 V ... The performance loss of CoB@MOF@CC could be ignored after 2500 h of OWS when the current density reached 500 mA cm⁻² ... FE value was close to 100%, with hydrogen and oxygen production rates of 8.93 and 4.46 μmol s⁻¹, respectively.

nodes.description: OWS performance in high-salt alkaline electrolyte
nodes.source_text: In the high-salt electrolyte, CoB@MOF@CC//CoB@MOF@CC required 1.62 V to reach a current density of 10 mA cm⁻² ... The chronopotentiometric curves indicated that the performance degradation at 100 mA cm⁻² was only 6.5% after 360 h of continuous catalysis.

nodes.description: OWS performance in real seawater alkaline electrolyte
nodes.source_text: The potential of CoB@MOF@CC//CoB@MOF@CC at 10 mA m⁻² was only 1.53 V in real seawater ... The durability at a current density of 100 mA cm⁻² was greater than 360 h, as the performance degradation was only 3.5%.

nodes.description: OWS performance in rainwater alkaline electrolyte
nodes.source_text: The potential for CoB@MOF@CC//CoB@MOF@CC under a rainwater environment at 10 mA cm⁻² was only 1.54 V ... The performance degradation was only 4% after 360 h at a current density of 100 mA m⁻².

nodes.description: OWS performance in urea alkaline electrolyte
nodes.source_text: The potential of CoB@MOF@CC//CoB@MOF@CC in a urea environment at 10 mA cm⁻² was only 1.53 V ... The performance degradation was only 4.5% after 360 h at a current density of 100 mA cm⁻².

nodes.characterization_summary: GIXRD patterns of CoB@MOF@CC show main diffraction peaks at 2θ = 13.4°, 18.4°, 29.0°, 37.8°, 50.7° corresponding to (112), (222), (125), (345), (466) planes of ZIF-67 with small shift vs MOF@CC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The main diffraction peaks for the crystalline CoB@MOF@CC electrode were located at 2θ = 13.4°, 18.4°, 29.0°, 37.8°, and 50.7°, which corresponded to the crystal planes of (112), (222), (125), (345), and (466), respectively, for the simulated ZIF-67 material.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoB@MOF@CC shows orderly dense bamboo leaf-like nanosheets with diameters ranging from 150 to 250 nm on CC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The microstructure of CoB@MOF@CC, with diameters ranging from 150 to 250 nm, was observed using SEM, which revealed orderly dense bamboo leaf-like nanosheets on the CC.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoB@MOF@CC has SSA of 10.35 m²/g compared to MOF@CC at 3.77 m²/g, showing 2.75 times stronger absorption-desorption capacity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared to the MOF@CC electrode (3.77 m²g⁻¹) CoB@MOF@CC had a larger SSA value of 10.35 m²g⁻¹ owing to the successful interspersion of amorphous transition metal borides.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoB@MOF shows bamboo leaf-like nano-layer in crystalline-amorphous form with width of 8-12 nm uniformly dispersed on surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM and high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images were employed to detect the diffraction patterns and calculate the lattice spacing of the CoB@MOF materials. Those results indicated that the bamboo leaf-like CoB@MOF nano-layer in the crystalline-amorphous form was uniformly dispersed on the surface with a width of 8-12 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringe of 0.243 nm corresponding to (345) crystal plane of simulated ZIF-67 with amorphous phase interfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The magnified region of the HRTEM image showed that the lattice fringe was 0.243 nm corresponding to the (3 4 5) crystal plane of the simulated ZIF67.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED patterns show distinct ring halo with diffraction ring sizes of 2.99, 2.43, and 1.87 Å corresponding to (125), (345), and (466) crystal planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the SAED patterns exhibited a distinct ring halo, wherein the diffraction ring sizes were 2.99, 2.43, and 1.87Å corresponding to the (125), (345), and (466) crystal planes, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping shows evenly dispersed B, C, N, O, and Co elements on CoB@MOF nanosheet surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) images showed evenly dispersed elements of B, C, N, O, and Co on the CoB@MOF nanosheet surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES shows original Co:B atomic ratio of ≈3.1:1 for CoB@MOF@CC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ICP-AES results revealed that the original Co:B atomic ratio was ≈3.1:1.

peaks at 778.5, 780.2, 781.4, 793.3, 795.8, and 797.2 eV were attributed to Co-B, Co³⁺, and Co²⁺ for Co 2p3/2, and Co-B, Co³⁺, and Co²⁺ for Co 2p1/2... B 1s spectrum... 185.2 eV (Co-B), 189.7 eV (B-N) and 191.7 eV (B-O)... O 1s spectrum... 530.7, 531.3, and 532.0 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoB@MOF@CC shows superhydrophilic surface with contact angle of almost 0° compared to Bare CC at 107.8° ± 0.8°.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the CoB@MOF@CC electrode possessed a superhydrophilic surface with a contact angle of almost zero (0°), indicating good wettability.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows D band at 1349 cm⁻¹ and G band at 1598 cm⁻¹ with I_D/I_G ratio of 0.99:1.00 indicating defective carbons.
nodes.evidence_snippet: There were two distinctive peaks for CoB@MOF@CC at 1349 and 1598 cm⁻¹ observed in the Raman spectrum, corresponding to the D band... and G band... The intensity ratio of I_D/I_G was maintained at around 0.99:1.00.

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR shows imidazole ring stretching 1350-1500 cm⁻¹, in-plane bending 1150-1300 cm⁻¹, Co-imidazole-N at 427 cm⁻¹, -OH at 3417 cm⁻¹, Co=O at 1625 cm⁻¹, Co-O²⁻ at 617 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FTIR spectrometry was employed to verify the functional groups... The wide peak from 1350 to 1500 cm⁻¹ was related to the stretching of the imidazole ring... an obvious peak at 427 cm⁻¹ corresponded to the Co-imidazole-N bond vibration mode.
